skill.name: merge-open-prs
skill.description: Snapshots selected open pull requests, assembles them into one native GitHub stack, resolves conflicts, verifies the combined result, and merges once.
skill.summary: Merge a verified set of open pull requests as one GitHub stack.
skill.author: jssblck

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command names, or read-only GitHub queries. Seven findings are confirmed because the workflow can rewrite branches, push rebased commits, prune local state, and merge pull requests; the unquoted branch placeholders also create a command-injection risk.

remediation.issue: Branch names are inserted as unquoted shell words before assignment to a quoted variable.
remediation.suggestion: Pass validated branch names as positional arguments or shell-array elements, and reject values that fail Git reference validation.

remediation.issue: Stack synchronization and rebasing can rewrite and push multiple pull request branches.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation that lists every affected branch and verified head SHA immediately before any rewrite or push.

remediation.issue: Merge and prune commands change remote and local repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Show the frozen work set, merge method, head SHAs, and cleanup targets before final execution. Keep administrative bypass disabled by default.

content.user_title: Merge Open Pull Requests as One Stack
content.value_statement: Merging several open pull requests together requires careful ordering, conflict handling, and repeated verification. This skill builds one GitHub stack and merges it through repository protections.
actual_capabilities: Snapshots all open pull requests or a user-selected subset before work begins.
Inspects changed files, branch relationships, checks, reviews, and repository merge policies.
Orders pull requests by dependencies, shared state, and change scope.
Builds or reuses a native GitHub pull request stack.
Guides conflict resolution and verifies the combined top-branch result.
Merges the verified stack once and reports all repository changes.
limitations: Native stacks require one repository, enabled stack support, and permission to update pull request branches.
The workflow depends on GitHub CLI stack commands and repository authentication.
It cannot bypass required checks, required reviews, rulesets, or merge queues.
Conflict resolution still requires project-specific judgment and repository test commands.

use_cases.title: Land a coordinated feature set
use_cases.description: Combine dependent pull requests into a verified stack and merge them as one repository change.

use_cases.title: Clear a release queue
use_cases.description: Order approved release pull requests, resolve shared-state conflicts, and verify the final release tree.

use_cases.title: Integrate maintenance updates
use_cases.description: Process related dependency, configuration, and tooling pull requests while preserving checks and review requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Merge every open pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge all currently open pull requests in this repository as one verified stack. Stop before rewriting branches that need separate approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a repository with a small open queue.

prompt_templates.title: Merge selected pull requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge pull requests {numbers} as one stack. Explain the order, verify required checks, and ignore pull requests opened after the snapshot.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused workflow for a user-selected work set.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve and merge a conflicting stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a stack from pull requests {numbers}. Resolve textual and semantic conflicts by layer, run relevant tests, then merge once.

prompt_templates.title: Manage a moving release stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge pull requests {numbers} using merge method {method}. Revalidate after default-branch changes, preserve head SHAs, and report every rewrite or bypass.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with strict policies and concurrent repository changes.

output_examples.output: Stopped before stack creation because two branches required rewriting. The report identified both branches and requested explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Land the open release pull requests after resolving conflicts.
output_examples.output: Resolved the lockfile and version conflicts on their owning layers, verified the combined tree, and merged the stack through the configured repository method.

best_practices: Freeze the work set and record every pull request head SHA before changing stack state.
Confirm stack membership, branch tips, checks, and repository policies immediately before merging.
Use a temporary worktree and disclose every branch rewrite, conflict resolution, and administrative action.
anti_patterns: Do not add pull requests that opened after the initial snapshot.
Do not push directly to the default branch or merge a multi-pull-request set individually.
Do not rewrite contributor branches or use administrative bypass without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill merge every open pull request automatically?
faq.answer: It snapshots all open pull requests unless you name a subset. Later arrivals are excluded from the work set.

faq.question: Can it merge pull requests from forks?
faq.answer: Native stack creation requires branches in one repository. Fork pull requests require the documented fallback and suitable permissions.

faq.question: How does it choose stack order?
faq.answer: User direction wins. Otherwise, isolated foundations go lower, dependencies follow them, and shared-state changes stay near the top.

faq.question: Will it bypass required checks or reviews?
faq.answer: No. Repository rules, required checks, reviews, strict update policies, and merge queues continue to control the merge.

faq.question: What happens when conflicts occur?
faq.answer: It resolves conflicts on the owning layer, rebases layers above it, and reruns checks for the combined result.

faq.question: Does it require approval before changing branches?
faq.answer: It requires explicit approval before rewriting branches you do not own. Administrative merge bypass also requires explicit approval and disclosure.
